turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, well, what finally made me come in is that I just keep forgetting basic adult things. Like, paying bills, returning interview emails, showing up for appointments... I even forgot to follow through on this one errand for my mom, which was so embarrassing because she asked me like three times. She always does that, though, asks me things when I'm right in the middle of something else, like when I was trying to organize my closet last week. I spent like four hours color-coding my shirts, but then I got distracted by this old box of photos and ended up looking through them all afternoon. Anyway, yeah, I keep forgetting important stuff, and it's starting to cost me real opportunities, like jobs and stuff. I just can't seem to keep it all straight.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes getting distracted from organizing their closet by an old box of photos.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient explicitly states they keep forgetting daily activities like paying bills, returning emails, keeping appointments, and running errands.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been having trouble with focus and remembering things — has this been going on since you were a kid, or did it start more recently?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, it's definitely been since I was a kid. Like, even back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright, but I constantly lost my worksheets. And they said I always rushed through directions and talked out of turn. My desk was a total disaster, too. It was so messy I could never find my assignments in there. 

I actually remember in fourth grade, my teacher made me stay inside during recess to clean it out, and I found like... three dried-up glue sticks and this massive collection of sparkly gel pens. Do you remember those? The ones that smelled like fruit? I was totally obsessed with them. I used to try to trade my lunch snacks for the blue ones because blue was my favorite color. I actually just started painting my bedroom blue last week. Well, I painted one wall, anyway. I ran out of painter's tape and had to go to the hardware store, but they had this huge display of succulents right by the door and I ended up looking at those for like an hour. Have you ever tried to keep a succulent alive? People say they're easy, but I swear I always overwater them and they just turn to mush. 

But um... wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? I totally lost my train of thought.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient notes that teachers said they 'always rushed through directions,' indicating a failure to give close attention to details.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient describes their childhood desk as a 'total disaster' and 'so messy I could never find my assignments.'
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient explicitly states they 'constantly lost my worksheets' in elementary school.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes being easily distracted by extraneous stimuli, such as looking at a display of succulents for an hour when they went to the store for painter's tape.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient recalls teachers noting that they frequently 'talked out of turn' in class.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech exhibits marked tangentiality, drifting from childhood report cards to gel pens, painting a bedroom, and succulents before completely losing their train of thought.

turns.doctor_question: You mentioned that this is costing you job opportunities — can you tell me more about how these attention and memory problems have affected your work life or relationships with other people?
turns.patient_response:
Um, yeah, work has been... well, it's been a disaster, honestly. I actually got fired from my last job recently because I just kept dropping the ball on things. And since then, it's like I can't even get it together to find a new one. I've missed, like, three interview follow-up emails just because I read them, tell myself I'll reply after I grab a snack, and then completely forget they exist. 

Speaking of snacks, I've been trying to learn how to bake sourdough bread since I've been unemployed. I bought all the stuff for a starter, and you have to feed it every day, which I actually remembered to do for almost a whole week! But then I left it on top of the fridge and it got this weird pink fuzzy mold on it. My roommate was so mad because it smelled awful. We actually get into a lot of arguments about the kitchen. She likes everything perfectly clean, but I'll start making dinner and then leave all the cabinets open and the ingredients out because I'll decide to go check the mail or something. 

But anyway, yeah, the job thing... I'm just unemployed right now. I even had to step back from this volunteer project I was doing at the animal shelter, which really sucked because I love dogs. I just kept forgetting my shifts or showing up two hours late. It just feels like I can't reliably manage the basic steps of moving my life forward right now. It's really frustrating.

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient describes failing to complete duties at work ('dropping the ball') and failing to finish tasks like making dinner or replying to emails.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient reports being easily distracted by extraneous stimuli or unrelated thoughts, such as abandoning dinner preparation to go check the mail.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient explicitly mentions forgetting daily activities, including interview follow-up emails, feeding a sourdough starter, and volunteer shifts.

turns.doctor_question: When you're sitting down trying to focus on something, like reading or working at a desk, do you find yourself fidgeting a lot, moving around in your chair, or feeling like you need to get up and move around?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, all the time. It's like... if I have to sit still for an interview, or a meeting, or even just watching a movie, I get this intense pressure inside my body. Like I absolutely have to get up, or shift around, or do something with my hands, otherwise I feel like I'm going to literally crawl out of my skin. 

Actually, speaking of movies, I tried to go to the theater last week to see that new sci-fi one. The one with the really cool aliens? I was so excited for it, I even bought my ticket in advance, which I never do. But the seats were those leather recliners, and normally those are great, right? Except this one had a weird squeak every time I moved, and I just could not stop shifting around. I was probably driving the guy next to me crazy. He kept giving me these sideways glances. He was eating popcorn, too, and he chewed so loudly. Have you ever noticed how loud popcorn is in a quiet theater? It's like, crunch, crunch, crunch. I can't stand it. I usually prefer gummy candy at the movies, like Peach Rings. But they didn't have Peach Rings at the concession stand, only those weird sour worms, and I hate sour stuff. It always makes my jaw tingle in a bad way. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Sitting at a desk? Yeah, I just... I can't stay still. It's really uncomfortable.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient is easily distracted by extraneous stimuli, such as a squeaky chair and the sound of someone chewing popcorn, which derails their train of thought.
symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient describes needing to 'do something with my hands' and 'could not stop shifting around' in their seat.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes an 'intense pressure inside my body' and feeling like they will 'literally crawl out of my skin' if they have to sit still.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from the topic of sitting still to a movie theater, popcorn, and gummy candy before forgetting the original question.

turns.doctor_question: When you were a child, did teachers or parents ever say you were hyperactive, or did you have trouble sitting still in class or at home — not just fidgeting, but like running around a lot or having difficulty waiting your turn?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, yeah, definitely. I mean, my mom always tells this story about how I literally ruined my cousin's birthday party when I was like six because I couldn't wait for him to blow out his candles, so I just blew them out myself. She said I was always running around the house like a tornado, climbing on the counters, just never, ever stopping. 

And honestly, the waiting thing hasn't really gotten better. Like, waiting for anything just makes me feel so... intensely impatient. If I'm waiting in a line at the grocery store, or even just waiting for a recruiter to call me back for an interview, it's agonizing. I just end up checking my phone over and over, or if I'm with people, like when I was doing that group volunteering at the shelter, I'd always end up interrupting people or just trying to push things along because I couldn't stand the waiting. 

It's actually why I stopped going to this one coffee shop near my apartment. They make really good lattes, like the kind with the actual latte art? The barista there used to make these little swans, which is so cool. I tried to learn how to do that at home once with my French press, but I just ended up spilling milk everywhere. My roommate was so mad because it got under the fridge and smelled like sour milk for a week. We had to use so much baking soda to get the smell out. Have you ever used baking soda for cleaning? It's actually amazing, you can mix it with vinegar and it fizzes up like a volcano. I used to make those paper mache volcanos for science fairs. I won third place once, but mostly because I used red food coloring in the vinegar so it looked like real lava. 

But um... yeah, waiting my turn. I'm just really bad at it. It drives me crazy.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes running around the house like a tornado and climbing on counters as a child.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient states they were 'never, ever stopping', indicating constant activity.
symptom_reasoning.S017: The patient explicitly confirms difficulty waiting their turn, citing examples like blowing out a cousin's candles and finding waiting in lines agonizing.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient admits to interrupting people when they become impatient.

turns.doctor_question: You've mentioned problems at work, with relationships, and with managing your responsibilities. Looking back over the past six months or so, would you say these attention and hyperactivity issues have been pretty much constantly affecting your life, or do they come and go?
turns.patient_response:
Um, it's pretty much constant. It's been like this for, gosh, about a year and two months now? It really started getting bad around the time everything started falling apart at my old job. I was working at this biotech startup, which sounded so cool when I took it. I thought I was going to be doing all this cutting-edge research, but it was mostly just entering data into these massive spreadsheets. 

Spreadsheets are the worst, honestly. The little cells just blur together after a while. My boss wanted everything color-coded, which I thought would be fun because I love organizing things by color. My whole closet is organized by the rainbow. I have this one section of just yellow sweaters, even though I don't really look good in yellow? It kind of washes me out. But they look so nice hanging there. I bought this mustard yellow cardigan at a thrift store once, and I found a five-dollar bill in the pocket. That was a great day. I bought a fancy coffee with it. 

But yeah, the biotech job... it started getting really bad then, and it just never stopped. Even after I got fired, it's just been a constant struggle every single day. So, definitely not coming and going. It's just always there.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient describes difficulty sustaining attention on tasks, noting that when entering data into spreadsheets, 'the little cells just blur together after a while.'
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates being easily distracted by unrelated thoughts, going on a long tangent about their closet, yellow sweaters, and a thrift store find before returning to the topic.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient talks excessively, providing a highly verbose and rambling response to a straightforward question about the timeline of their symptoms.

turns.doctor_question: You've told me about problems at work and at home with your roommate. Have you also noticed these attention and hyperactivity issues showing up in other situations, like when you're with friends, in social settings, or doing things you enjoy?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, definitely. It's like... even when I'm supposed to be relaxing or doing something fun, I just can't do the quiet thing. Like, if I try to read a book, or do that meditation stuff everyone says is so good for you, or even just sit calmly with my friends at a park, I can't just *be*. I end up tapping my foot, or humming, or talking over people, or pulling out my phone to check something because being still and quiet is just... impossible. 

Actually, my friend Sarah tried to get me into meditation last month. She has this whole setup in her apartment with a singing bowl and these floor cushions. They're velvet, which I usually love. I have this velvet jacket I got for a concert once. It was an outdoor concert, and it started pouring rain, and the velvet got totally ruined. It smelled like wet dog for weeks, which is weird because I don't even have a dog. I want a dog, though. Maybe a golden retriever? They always look so happy. But I don't think my apartment allows dogs, just cats. And I'm allergic to cats. My eyes get all puffy and red, like I've been crying for days. 

But yeah, the meditation thing... I lasted maybe two minutes before I started humming a song that was stuck in my head, and Sarah got so annoyed. So quiet activities are basically a no-go for me.

symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient mentions tapping their foot when trying to sit calmly.
symptom_reasoning.S013: The patient explicitly states they cannot do 'the quiet thing' and finds it impossible to be still and quiet during leisure activities like reading or meditating.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient notes that they end up 'talking over people' when trying to relax with friends.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from a story about meditation cushions to a velvet jacket, a concert, wet dogs, and cat allergies before returning to the original topic.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever been formally evaluated or diagnosed with ADHD, or have you ever been on medication for attention or hyperactivity problems?
turns.patient_response:
Um, no, I've never been officially tested for it or anything. And I've never taken any medication for it, either. I mean, my mom used to joke about giving me coffee when I was little to calm me down, because she read somewhere that caffeine does the opposite for hyper kids? But she never actually did it. I didn't start drinking coffee until college, mostly because the dining hall coffee was so bad. It tasted like burnt dirt. But then I discovered iced lattes, and it was game over. I probably spend way too much money on iced lattes now. 

I actually tried to make my own syrups at home to save money. I made this brown sugar vanilla one, and it was really good for like two days, but then it crystallized in the fridge and turned into a solid rock. I couldn't even get it out of the jar. I had to throw the whole mason jar away, which sucked because I use those jars for my overnight oats. Do you like overnight oats? I put chia seeds in mine, but they always get stuck in my teeth. It's so embarrassing when you're talking to someone and you just have a giant black seed right in the front. I had that happen on a date once. He didn't even tell me! I went to the bathroom halfway through dinner and saw it, and I wanted to die. We didn't go out again. 

But um, no, no official diagnosis or pills or anything like that. Just me trying to deal with it, I guess.
